entries.original: As in 11.2.1 the map theta(x)=-x′ is an automorphism of L, but this time it satisfies theta(e_r)=e_{-r} for each root r. To show that the fundamental co-roots and the root vectors e_r form a Chevalley basis we observe that theta(ie_r)=-(-ie_{-r}) and that [ie_r,-ie_{-r}]=h_r. Thus the fundamental co-roots together with ie_r (r positive) and -ie_{-r} (r positive) form a Chevalley basis, as in 11.2.1. It follows that the fundamental co-roots together with e_r,e_{-r} (r positive) also form a Chevalley basis, using the general ideas of section 4.2.
entries.corrected: After [h_r e_r]=2e_r: As in 11.2.1 the map theta(x)=-x′ is an automorphism of L satisfying theta(e_r)=-e_{-r} for each root r. Thus the fundamental co-roots together with the root vectors e_r form a Chevalley basis, by the argument of 11.2.1.
entries.reason: The imaginary rescaling detour rests on E045 and is false for the displayed matrices. With r=epsilon1-epsilon2, s=epsilon2-epsilon3, the displayed basis has [e_r,e_s]=e_{r+s}; scaling all positive-root vectors by i produces structure constant i, not plus/minus 1. The corrected transpose sign directly gives N_{-r,-s}=-N_{r,s}. Together with the normalized co-roots and 4.1.2 this gives N_{r,s}=plus/minus(p+1), exactly the valid argument of 11.2.1. No imaginary rescaling is needed. This is an explicit proof repair, not just punctuation; full original paragraph retained here.
entries.status: corrected; source paragraph checked, exact D4/D5 counterexamples and general replacement argument

entries.original: B_l(K) is isomorphic to the orthogonal group POmega_(2l+1)(K,f_B), with no exception in the statement.
entries.corrected: Qualify the identification by except for B_2(2).
entries.reason: The proof explicitly excludes B2(2) on printed page 187. Carter 11.1 identifies B2(2) with S6. Omega is defined here as the commutator subgroup, so Omega5(2) is A6, of order 360, while B2(2) has order 720. Exact enumeration of the printed five-dimensional generators over F2 gives order 720, centre 1, derived subgroup order 360 with centre 1, and faithful symplectic projection of order 720. Geck–Malle 2020 Table 2.1 independently gives Sp4(2)=S6. Thus the missing exception is substantive and required; no change to the existing proof exclusion.
entries.status: corrected; source proof, literature and exact Sage diagnostic agree

entries.location: 13.5.1 proof, nontrivial fixed element for B2/G2 equivalence classes

The highest-root pairs (2a+b, a+b) and (3a+2b, 2a+b), a short, b long, have no positive integral combination that is a root. The commutator formula and uniqueness of root factorization give the replacement. Steinberg 2016, Lemma 61 (printed 104), explicitly uses a product over a terminal-root orbit. Exact root checks in twisted-fixed-sage.json and a conditional abstract group proof in TwistedOrbit.lean; neither formalizes the entire BN-pair theorem.

entries.original: For any root r and any permitted nonzero t one can find a self-conjugate K-character of Q with chi(r)=t; later chi(r)=lambda is prescribed arbitrarily.
entries.corrected: Use explicit orbit coroot characters to obtain only the nontrivial root values needed. For an A2 orbit choose chi=chi_(r,lambda)chi_(rbar,lambdabar),so chi(r)=lambda^2/lambdabar and chi(r+rbar)=lambda*lambdabar.
entries.reason: The assertion of arbitrary values fails: over GF(25), 24 self-conjugate Q-characters give only 8 root values. For fixed singleton roots c^2 suffices except over GF(3); in that finite residual case an adjacent orbit gives an inverse norm with both values nonzero. Commuting orbits give c^2 over K, which has more than 3 elements. For A2, the norm is nonconstant unless the fixed field is GF(2). These constructions give exactly the nontrivial characters used below. Steinberg 2016, printed 112, gives the same unitary torus weights. Sage verifies the symbolic commutator/inverse and bounded finite cases, not the full theorem. The 1989 reprint adds a Supplement, Hartley’s Lemma, which refers to this page and states which values chi(r) occur: every t (every t = tbar if r = rbar), except t^2 for 2A3 and 2D_l and t^3 for 2A2 with q ≡ -1 mod 3 when r ≠ rbar, and t^2 for 2G2 at r = a+b, 3a+b. This agrees with the correction (2A2 over GF(25): only cubes, 8 values). An exact Sage computation of the value group for every root confirms the lemma for 2A_l (2 ≤ l ≤ 7), 2D_l (4 ≤ l ≤ 7), 2E6 and 3D4 with 15 values of q up to 32, 2B2 and 2F4 up to GF(2^11) and GF(2^9), 2G2 up to GF(3^7), and a direct enumeration over 24 small fields; the printed page 263 is unchanged in 1989.
entries.status: corrected; source, stated validation evidence and the 1989 Supplement checked

A genuine conjugation-compatible witness over GF(4), t = u = 1, v^2 + v = 1, gives difference 1. The first factor x_S3(t·vbar) retains its bar.

entries.original: Thus the subgroup of Omega_2l(K,f_D) of elements T invariant under sigma is S Omega_2l(K0,f) S^-1. Since G is isomorphic to P Omega_2l(K,f_D) it follows that G1 is isomorphic to P Omega_2l(K0,f).
entries.corrected: The fixed root subgroups generating U1, V1 become elementary orthogonal subgroups of f over K0; these generate Omega_2l(K0,f). Their generated matrix group is S Omega_2l(K0,f) S^-1; quotienting by scalar matrices gives the stated identification.
entries.reason: Fixed points do not in general commute with taking the commutator subgroup. Over K0 = GF(3), K = GF(9), the matrix diag(2,1,1,1,2,1,1,1) preserves the descended form and is fixed, with spinor norm 2. It belongs to Omega over K, since 2 becomes a square, but not over K0. Taylor 11.51 supplies the spinor-norm criterion. The definition of G1 uses fixed root groups, not all fixed elements; Taylor 11.46 gives elementary/Siegel generation. Sage checks that the terminal D4 orbit product is exactly a Siegel transformation, as well as the quadratic pullback and semilinear descent in characteristics 0 and 2. The full general identification is not formally proved.
entries.status: corrected; source and stated validation evidence checked

entries.reason: The prepended word has s+1 letters. The exchange index j in 2..s+1 corresponds to alpha = j-1 in 1..s. Common first generators require alpha = 1; in S3 the equal reduced words (a,b), (a,b), a = (12), b = (23), admit only alpha = 1. A Sage exact counterexample and 8 finite exchange cases passed. Lean checks the conditional deletion identity and common-first cancellation, not the whole Matsumoto theorem.

entries.location: 15.6.2, paragraph proving preservation of minimal galleries from A
entries.original: The restriction retr_(Sigma,C′): Sigma′ → Sigma is the unique isomorphism fixing all faces of C′.
entries.corrected: Use distance from a face to a chamber; apartment and global distances coincide by retraction. A retraction centred at E preserves distances from any face of E, by restriction to an apartment containing E and the target chamber. Both factors of alpha preserve distance from A, so minimal galleries from A remain minimal.
entries.reason: C′ is not in Σ′, which contains C and C″. The stated restriction sends both C and C″ to C, so it cannot be injective. This already fails in a rank-one thick building. The corrected distance argument is exactly the missing ingredient of the parallel proof in Abramenko–Brown 4.131, using 4.34/4.35/4.39(2). It uses only retractions and the thin apartment axioms, not the conclusion that apartments are Coxeter. The conclusion and the rest of Carter’s proof are unchanged.
entries.status: corrected; full source checked; literature corroborated proof repair
